cards.title: Introduction to Flask Deployment
cards.content:
When developing a Flask application, you typically use the built-in development server (app.run()). However, this server is not suitable for production because it is not designed to handle high loads, lacks security features, and does not scale well.

To deploy a Flask app to production, you need a WSGI server (like Gunicorn or uWSGI) behind a Reverse Proxy (like Nginx) running on a production-ready environment such as a Linux VPS or a cloud platform.

cards.title: Preparing Your Flask App
cards.content:
Before deploying, you must make several changes to your Flask application:

  • Debug Mode: Ensure debug=False in production to prevent leaking sensitive traceback information.
  • Environment Variables: Use libraries like python-dotenv or OS environment variables to manage secrets (database URIs, secret keys).
  • Requirements File: Generate a pinned dependency file using pip freeze > requirements.txt.
# Example production run configuration
if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8000)

cards.title: Setting Up Gunicorn
cards.content:
Gunicorn (Green Unicorn) is a pure-Python WSGI HTTP server. It is pre-cloned and ported from Ruby's Unicorn project.

Install Gunicorn in your virtual environment:

pip install gunicorn

Run your Flask application with Gunicorn by specifying the module and app instance:

gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:8000 wsgi:app

Here, -w 4 specifies 4 worker processes to handle concurrent requests.

cards.title: Configuring Nginx Reverse Proxy
cards.content:
Nginx sits in front of Gunicorn. It handles incoming client requests, serves static files directly (improving performance), and manages SSL certificates.

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name example.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    }
}
